summary: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai, and the University of Göttingen, also studying under Martin Haug. He held professorships at Elphinstone College and Deccan College, and was Vice Chancellor of Mumbai University.

Ramaprasad Chanda worked in Indology and archaeology. Educated at Scottish Church College, he taught history at Hindu School and Rajshahi Collegiate School, lectured at the University of Calcutta, worked for the Archaeological Survey of India, and served at the Indian Museum (1921–1932).

Ramaranjan Mukherji was an Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. He served as Sanskrit department head at Jadavpur University (1956), vice chancellor at Burdwan and Rabindra Bharati universities, and chancellor of National Sanskrit University (~2005–2010).
Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist. He held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at S. L. D. Arts College (attested 1938) and at Gujarat Vidyapith.

Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai and Heidelberg University. He served as professor and Arts Dean at Savitribai Phule Pune University, taught at Fergusson College, and was Honorary Secretary of Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1939–2001).

Ramesh Chandra Majumdar was an historian and Indologist who studied at Calcutta and Presidency universities. He served as professor and vice chancellor at the University of Dhaka (1921–1942), and held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Nagpur University, and in the United States.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Attested in 1967, he was head of History & Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest University, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State University.

Ramin Etesami is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at International Buddhist College (attested 2015), where he studied under Geshe Lozang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina.
Ramon N. Prats is a scholar in Tibetology. He held affiliations with Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017).
Randall Studstill is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who studied under doctoral supervisor Richard K. Payne and teacher Steven D. Goodman.

Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist and sinologist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley under James Alan Matisoff. He served as a professor at City University of Hong Kong (~1996–2008) and at Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai (2021).

Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at The University of Hong Kong, supervised by Jing Yin and co-supervised by Kakkapalliye Anuruddha Thera, having also studied under traditional teacher Attaragama Gnanawimala.

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under teachers including Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Karsé Kongtrul, and the 13th Dalai Lama, and taught numerous disciples.

Raniero Gnoli was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Mario Praz. He served as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who held a professorship in Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003, 2017).
Raphael Kühner was a linguist who studied at Ernestinum Gotha and the University of Göttingen (~1821–1825).
Raphael von Koeber was a philosopher who studied at the Moscow Conservatory, the University of Jena (~1878–1881), and Heidelberg University. He held a post at the University of Tokyo in 1893.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Fergusson College under Ramchandra Dattatrya Ranade, Muni Jinvijaya, and Sukhlal Sanghvi, and served as Professor of Sanskrit and Ancient Indian History at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1930).

Rasmus Rask was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Odense Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen. At the University of Copenhagen, he held posts as librarian and professor of Eastern languages and literary history.
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, whom he succeeded in 2017.
